brief: Arteo is a small creative studio in Nitra: websites, visual identities and print. The new site is built on a risograph idea: two print inks, blue and fluorescent pink, overlap and slip out of register. The logo has to belong to that world, replace the old green three-circle mark and work from a 16 px browser tab to a studio sign.
criteria: Success: unmistakably Arteo, legible as 'arteo' at a glance, recognisable at 16 px as 'ar', works in one colour, and the two inks feel native to the riso website.

concepts.name: Ligature
concepts.idea: The 'a' and the 'r' share one stroke, and where they meet the two inks overprint into a third colour.
rationale: Craft you can see: a ligature is a typographer's detail, built from circles and straight stems, not a stock font
The overprint at the shared stem is the website's riso idea in one spot of colour
The 'ar' symbol stands on its own for favicons, avatars and app icons
Works in one colour; a heavier cut keeps it clear at 16 px

recommendation: Use the wordmark as the primary logo and the 'ar' symbol wherever space is square or tiny.
next_steps: Swap the logo and favicon on arteo.sk
Update the Arteo design system and Figma file
Trademark and domain-handle check before print
